note: The Bailiwick of Guernsey keeps the United Kingdom's visa requirements within the Common Travel Area (a UK visit visa admits a visitor), and since 23 April 2026 its own electronic travel authorisation for non-visa nationals coming from outside the UK and Islands: the gb list.

sources.title: States of Guernsey, Passports and Immigration
sources.said: From 23rd April 2026 an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) became a requirement for non-visa nationals travelling to the Bailiwick of Guernsey. ... The Bailiwick of Guernsey is part of the Common Travel Area (CTA), along with the other Channel Islands, the Isle of Man, Republic of Ireland and the UK and therefore maintains the same standard of immigration controls. If you have a UK visit visa, then this will also allow you to visit the Bailiwick of Guernsey and the other Crown Dependencies (Jersey and the Isle of Man). You do not need a separate visa*.

sources.title: Home Office, Common Travel Area guidance (GOV.UK)
sources.said: Each CTA jurisdiction is largely responsible for decisions on who can enter and stay. The Crown Dependencies have almost identical visa requirements to that of the UK. ... Each Crown Dependency (Jersey, Guernsey and Isle of Man) has introduced their own legally distinct ETA schemes.
